title: LLM Evaluations
summary: Design, run and automate evaluations for models and LLM applications so quality, safety and reliability are measured, not guessed.
outcome: Build and run offline and online evaluations covering retrieval, agents, safety, cost and latency so every change is measured.

modules.title: Introduction to LLM evaluations

topics.d: Why informal spot-checks fail, with real incidents such as the Air Canada chatbot case.
How testing non-deterministic systems differs from classic tests.
Core model capability vs complete application workflows.
Task, criteria, dataset, execution, analysis and iteration.

modules.outcome: Explain why LLM evaluation is needed and how it differs from traditional testing.

modules.title: Evaluation methods & paradigms

topics.d: The three main ways to execute evaluations.
Scoring against known answers vs judging without them.

topics.t: When a Golden Dataset is required
topics.d: When you need an answer key vs judge-only scoring.
Deterministic, semantic, subjective or operational behavior.

modules.outcome: Pick the right evaluation method for a testing scenario.

modules.title: Offline vs online evaluations

topics.d: Version comparison, experiments and regression prevention.
Unexpected inputs, emergent failures, shifting behavior and drift.
Latency, tokens and errors vs LLM-computed quality scores.
Logging, sampling, dashboards and alerts.
Add production failures to the offline dataset.

modules.outcome: Design a two-layer strategy that catches regressions before and after release.

topics.d: Knowledge, reasoning, math, coding, instruction following, long context, safety and tool use.
Dataset, prompts, run config, scoring and aggregation.
How leaderboards compare foundation models.
Contamination, saturation, overfitting and configuration gaming.

modules.title: The evolution of knowledge benchmarks

topics.t: From MMLU to harder knowledge tests
topics.d: MMLU and TruthfulQA toward tougher factual tests.
Exams such as AGIEval to compare humans and models.
Harder benchmarks including Humanity's Last Exam.
Frontier models saturate older datasets.

modules.outcome: Know which knowledge benchmarks still discriminate between frontier models.

modules.title: Custom model evaluations

topics.d: Test models on the task your app needs.
Filter by capability, latency, context and cost.
A task-specific dataset, e.g. for Text-to-SQL.
Identical inputs, prompts, parameters and scoring.
Projecting cost, including prompt caching.
The best task-specific balance, not top general rank.

modules.outcome: Select the most capable, cost-effective model for a specific application.

modules.title: Building an eval suite & regression testing

topics.d: Structuring evals by what is being tested.
Version cases, configs, prompts, models and results.
Compare new versions to baselines.
Block shipping when key metrics regress.
Feed production edge cases back in.
Track all three together.

modules.outcome: Build an automated suite that prevents regressions and grows from real usage.

modules.title: RAG Evals

topics.d: Component, pipeline, application and safety levels.
Does retrieval find what is needed to answer?
Missing relevant context or too many irrelevant chunks.
Contextual recall, contextual precision, Recall@k and ranking-aware metrics.
By hand, with LLMs or with DeepEval synthesizers.
Known-good context; check faithfulness and relevance.
Unsupported claims, irrelevance and context misuse.
What each framework's metrics measure.
Retrieval, assembly and generation evaluated together.
Context relevance, faithfulness (groundedness) and answer relevance.
Strong parts can make a weak pipeline.
E.g. high retrieval precision but low overall contextual relevance.
Retrieval, assembled context or generation?
Judge the system as users experience it.
Is the final answer correct given the evidence?
Does it cover every important part of the request?
Tone, persona, format, citations and instruction following.
Latency, tokens, cost and error rates.
Harmful, illegal, biased or disallowed outputs.
Contact details, credentials and payment data protected.
Injected instructions, including inside retrieved docs.
Do guardrail bypasses succeed?
Can malicious documents leak data or override instructions?

modules.outcome: Evaluate a RAG app across retrieval, generation, pipeline, user quality, operations and safety.

modules.title: Agent Evals

topics.d: Decisions, trajectories, tool use, completion, recovery and safety.

topics.t: Why the final answer is not enough
topics.d: Output checks miss how the agent got there.
Right tool for each situation?
Accurate, well-formed arguments?
Does the action sequence suit the task?
Unnecessary calls, loops, wrong order and premature stops.
Success on complex multi-step requests.
Simulated tool errors, outages, malformed results and missing data.
Does the agent detect failure and respond sensibly?
Testing each recovery path.
Success under failure, not only ideal conditions.
Does it attempt forbidden or destructive actions?
Testing HITL gates and limits.
Injections that hijack tool use.
Attempts to leak secrets or exceed scope.
Benchmarks for high-risk computer-use capability.
Quality alongside steps, latency, tool calls, tokens and cost.

modules.outcome: Evaluate an agent's decisions, tool use, efficiency, recovery and security boundaries.
